parsed.elsewhere_quote:
We have the following self-duality property:
\[
S\in\mathcal F
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
S\cap R\ne\varnothing\text{ for every }R\in\mathcal F.
\tag{1}
\]
parsed.explanation: The omitted direction of (2) is an immediate consequence of the already proved (1). If S contains C∈C⊆F, then C meets every R∈F by (1), so S also meets every R∈F; applying (1) again gives S∈F. A separate upward-closedness lemma or sentence is unnecessary, and L6.1 is explicitly established through self-duality.
